previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old woman with a history of pancreas and kidney transplants, mechanical mitral valve replacement, and systolic heart failure was admitted for worsening dyspnea and leg swelling. She had recently completed treatment for pneumonia and was found to have acute kidney injury on chronic kidney disease, leading to significant fluid overload. Her heart function had improved since her last admission, with ejection fraction increasing to 35%. She was managed with hemodialysis after placement of a tunneled internal jugular catheter and underwent laparoscopic placement of a peritoneal dialysis catheter for future home dialysis. Her immunosuppressant levels were optimized, and she was restarted on warfarin. She improved clinically, with resolution of pulmonary edema and stabilization of renal function, and was discharged home to continue outpatient hemodialysis while the PD catheter matured.
problems: Heart valve replaced by other means

symptoms of infection currently, though reports abdominal

discharge. Pt has no evidence of SBP based on peritoneal fluid

this very fever is from atelectasis or renal graft rejection.

peritoneal catheter site infection, to be continued for total of 
7 days. Blood, peritoneal, and urine cultures have all been 
negative so far.

constipation. KUB showed reduced bowel gas, possibly stool 
loading. Radiologist suggested possibilty of bowel ischemia,
